@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+import matplotlib
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import seaborn.objects as so
+
+
+def report(name, fig):
+    axes = fig.axes
+    for ax in axes:
+        print(name, "xlim=", ax.get_xlim(), "ylim=", ax.get_ylim(),
+              "xgrid=", any(l.get_visible() for l in ax.get_xgridlines()),
+              "ygrid=", any(l.get_visible() for l in ax.get_ygridlines()),
+              "yinv=", ax.yaxis_inverted())
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+df = pd.DataFrame({"cat": ["a", "b", "c"], "val": [1, 2, 3]})
+
+# 1. Explicit Nominal on x
+p1 = so.Plot(df, x="cat", y="val").add(so.Dot()).scale(x=so.Nominal())
+report("explicit-x", p1.plot())
+
+# 2. Inferred Nominal on x (string -> Nominal)
+p2 = so.Plot(df, x="cat", y="val").add(so.Dot())
+report("inferred-x", p2.plot())
+
+# 3. Nominal on y -> should be inverted
+p3 = so.Plot(df, x="val", y="cat").add(so.Dot()).scale(y=so.Nominal())
+report("explicit-y", p3.plot())
+
+# 4. Inferred Nominal on y
+p4 = so.Plot(df, x="val", y="cat").add(so.Dot())
+report("inferred-y", p4.plot())
+
+# 5. User forces grid -> grid should stay
+p5 = (so.Plot(df, x="cat", y="val").add(so.Dot())
+      .theme({"axes.grid": True}))
+report("forced-grid", p5.plot())
+
+# 6. Numeric x unaffected by nominal logic
+p6 = so.Plot(df, x="val", y="val").add(so.Dot())
+report("numeric", p6.plot())

diff --git a/tests/_core/test_nominal_axis.py b/tests/_core/test_nominal_axis.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..983304538010d4308006dcda336fe2849cde1f19
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/_core/test_nominal_axis.py
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+"""Regression tests: Nominal scales drawn like categorical axes.
+
+Covers the three behaviors requested in the issue:
+1. limits span first level - 0.5 .. last level + 0.5 (no normal margin logic)
+2. no grid drawn (even though the default style enables one)
+3. the y axis is inverted
+plus deferring to an explicit theme grid request, and inferred nominal scales.
+
+These call ``Plotter._finalize_figure`` directly, which is the documented
+place for this behavior. Going through ``Plot.plot()`` would also run the
+mark, and mark plotting currently raises in this environment because pandas
+no longer provides the ``mode.use_inf_as_null`` option that
+``Plotter._setup_split_generator`` enters. That is a separate, pre-existing
+environment incompatibility and is not what these tests are about.
+"""
+import matplotlib
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+
+import matplotlib as mpl
+import pytest
+
+from seaborn._core.plot import Plot, Plotter
+from seaborn._core.scales import Nominal
+
+
+def _make_plotter(theme=None):
+    return Plotter(pyplot=False, theme=theme or {})
+
+
+def _finalize(scales, limits=None, theme=None):
+    """Run _finalize_figure on a fresh plotter with the given scales."""
+    p = Plot()
+    p._scales = dict(scales)
+    if limits is not None:
+        p._limits = limits
+    plotter = _make_plotter(theme)
+    plotter._figure = mpl.figure.Figure()
+    plotter._subplots = [{
+        "ax": plotter._figure.add_subplot(111),
+        "x": "x",
+        "y": "y",
+    }]
+    plotter._finalize_figure(p)
+    return plotter._subplots[0]["ax"]
+
+
+def _nominal(levels):
+    scale = Nominal()
+    scale._units_seed = list(levels)
+    return scale
+
+
+def _grid_visible(ax, which):
+    lines = ax.get_xgridlines() if which == "x" else ax.get_ygridlines()
+    return any(line.get_visible() for line in lines)
+
+
+def test_nominal_x_limits_half_step_around_levels():
+
+    ax = _finalize({"x": _nominal(["a", "b", "c"])})
+    assert ax.get_xlim() == (-0.5, 2.5)
+
+
+def test_nominal_x_hides_grid():
+
+    # Even though the active style would show a grid, nominal hides it.
+    ax = _finalize({"x": _nominal(["a", "b", "c"])})
+    assert not _grid_visible(ax, "x")
+
+
+def test_nominal_y_is_inverted_and_hides_grid():
+
+    ax = _finalize({"y": _nominal(["a", "b", "c"])})
+    assert ax.yaxis_inverted()
+    assert ax.get_ylim() == (2.5, -0.5)
+    assert not _grid_visible(ax, "y")
+
+
+def test_nominal_grid_restored_by_explicit_theme():
+
+    # A user-supplied theme that asks for a grid must win over the default
+    # nominal suppression: with grid pre-enabled, it stays visible.
+    plotter = _make_plotter({"axes.grid": True})
+    plotter._figure = mpl.figure.Figure()
+    ax = plotter._figure.add_subplot(111)
+    ax.grid(True, axis="x")  # emulate the active style enabling the grid
+    plotter._subplots = [{"ax": ax, "x": "x", "y": "y"}]
+
+    p = Plot()
+    p._scales = {"x": _nominal(["a", "b", "c"])}
+    plotter._finalize_figure(p)
+
+    assert ax.get_xlim() == (-0.5, 2.5)
+    assert _grid_visible(ax, "x")
+
+
+def test_nominal_respects_explicit_limits():
+
+    ax = _finalize({"x": _nominal(["a", "b", "c"])}, limits={"x": (0, 1)})
+    assert ax.get_xlim() == (0, 1)
+
+
+def test_numeric_scale_is_untouched():
+
+    from seaborn._core.scales import Continuous
+
+    ax = _finalize({"x": Continuous()})
+    # No nominal handling should apply: normal margins remain in force.
+    assert ax.get_xlim() != (-0.5, 2.5)
